tables.title: Employee wages by industry, monthly, unadjusted for seasonality
tables.usedFor: Average hourly wage, median hourly wage, and average weekly wage for employees aged 15 and over, both full- and part-time, all industries. Provincial rows are the average hourly wage on the same cut.

adapted: 12-month and 1-month percent changes on CPI indexes are calculated by Canadian Data Insights from the published index levels. They are not a separate Statistics Canada percent-change series.
The seasonally adjusted 1-month change is calculated the same way from table 18-10-0006-01.
CPI-trim, CPI-median, and CPI-common are the published year-over-year percent changes in table 18-10-0256-01.

Approximate percentage-point contributions multiply the 2025 basket weight by the calculated 12-month component change and divide by 100. They are not Statistics Canada's published contributions, and they are shown only for the eight major components, which partition the basket. Energy, gasoline, goods, and services overlap those components and are not added in.
Real wage changes divide the wage ratio by the all-items CPI ratio over the same 12 months. The result is calculated here.
The purchasing-power calculator multiplies a dollar amount by the latest monthly all-items index and divides by the chosen year's published annual average all-items index. Both indexes are 2002=100.

The personal calculator is a weighted average of the eight published major-component 12-month changes, using either the latest basket weights or shares entered on the page. It is not the official Consumer Price Index.
